solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Where peer may sit, in Lords, returned to power (10)

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the House of Lords is a parliamentary chamber
TO kept as it stands plus P for power, before turning round

annotation.surface: A nobleman taking his seat in the Lords as his party regains office.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is in the definition: a peer is a nobleman, but read as 'pee-er' he is someone who pees.
annotation.definitionFit: A bedroom potty kept under the bed is where someone needing to pee at night would sit, so a punning 'pee-er' sits there.

entries.clue: Line featured in very bad European account (9)

indicators.note: a thing featured in something else appears within it, so the line sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: chronic is informal British for dreadful

annotation.surface: A report that fiercely criticises some European's writing, with one line singled out.
annotation.walkthrough: The L sits between CHRONIC and E, so it is inside the pair taken together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a historical record setting events down in the order they happened is a written account.

entries.clue: Ascendant bird is source of magic in primitive religion (7)

indicators.note: something ascendant is rising, so in a down clue the bird is read upwards
the source of a river is where it begins, so take just the first letter

blocks.note: the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

annotation.surface: A soaring bird held to be the fount of magic in an early faith.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a verb joining the halves of the sentence but is simply IS in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The belief that spirits dwell in trees, rivers and animals is typical of early tribal faiths, hence called primitive.

entries.clue: Adele ultimately inclined to throttle pub trumpeter (8)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter of Adele
throttling is gripping round the throat, so the pub goes inside the other word

blocks.note: leant = inclined; it holds the pub
PH = public house on a map

annotation.surface: The singer Adele, eventually minded to strangle a trumpet player in a bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' wants to be a musician in Adele's world; it is the animal that trumpets.
annotation.definitionFit: The loud call this big grey beast makes through its trunk is called trumpeting, so it earns the name by sound.

entries.clue: Motel being one in road, we turn to map when lost (11,4)

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer by example: motel is one portmanteau word

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered from their places, so they come out in a new order

annotation.surface: Lost drivers stop at a motel on the road and turn to the map.
annotation.walkthrough: A motel is a motor hotel: two words blended into one.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: motel fuses motor and hotel, the kind of blended coinage Lewis Carroll named after a two-part suitcase.

entries.clue: Second-rate cash prize (6)

blocks.note: tin is old slang for money
the pot is the prize money in a game

annotation.surface: A cheap and shoddy award of money.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a second prize in a contest, but 'Second-rate' is the definition standing alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pot made of cheap tin became a byword for anything shabby or petty, as in a tinpot dictator.

entries.clue: Artist losing urge, knocked back wine (4)

indicators.note: an artist losing something no longer has it, so those letters come out
a drink knocked back is thrown back, so the urge is turned round before it goes

blocks.note: a yen is an urge; knocked back it is NEY, which Hockney loses

annotation.surface: A painter giving up drinking and then downing some wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back wine' reads as a drink downed; 'knocked back' belongs to the urge, and wine is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the British name for German white Rhine vintages, from the town of Hochheim.

entries.clue: Games packed in Orcadian island with any luck (9)

indicators.note: the games and packed pieces are placed in the island, inside its letters

blocks.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands; it holds PEFULL

annotation.surface: Sports crammed on to a remote Orkney island, fingers crossed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Packed' seems to be the container word, but it is FULL, and 'in' does the packing. Orcadian means from Orkney, off the north of Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as a sentence adverb: saying it expresses a wish that things turn out well.

entries.clue: Canal company introduces arrangement of locks (4,3)

indicators.note: whoever introduces a guest goes first, so the company comes before the canal

blocks.note: a crew is a company of workers
a cut is a man-made waterway

annotation.surface: A waterways firm brings in a new system of canal locks.
annotation.walkthrough: Canal locks are the surface; the locks are hair.
annotation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses of hair, and this very short, bristly men's style is one way of arranging them.

entries.clue: Northern residents reportedly ruled this place in the East End (8)

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so go by the sound of the words

blocks.clueFragment: this place in the East End
blocks.note: here, with the H dropped as in Cockney speech

annotation.surface: People up north are said to have governed round these parts of London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Residents' suggests people; they are animals of the Arctic. The East End of London drops its H's, so here becomes 'ere.
annotation.definitionFit: These antlered deer live wild in Lapland, Siberia and the Arctic tundra, so they are residents of the far north.

entries.clue: Lacking sleep, son leaves city (6)

indicators.note: when someone leaves they depart, so the son's letter goes from the word

annotation.surface: A sleep-deprived son moves away from the city.
annotation.walkthrough: NAPLESS means lacking sleep; the son leaving takes one of its S's.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the southern Italian port beneath Vesuvius, capital of Campania.

entries.clue: Nothing to cover area one’s quick to protect (4)

indicators.note: a cover goes over and round what it hides, so the nothing wraps the area

blocks.note: nil = nothing; it holds the A

annotation.surface: Someone eager to guard an area with no cover at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like an adjective for someone speedy; it is the tender flesh under a nail.
annotation.definitionFit: The quick is the sensitive flesh at a fingertip, and the hard plate growing over it exists to shield it.

entries.clue: Government department put female in igloo? (4,6)

indicators.note: to put something is to place it, here the female letter
the female letter is placed in the igloo phrase, inside its letters

blocks.note: an igloo is a dwelling made of ice

annotation.surface: A ministry deciding to house a woman in an Inuit snow hut.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'igloo' is defined by a playful description, home of ice, rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the British ministry responsible for policing, immigration and security.

entries.clue: Wine store in future undergoing merger? (9)

indicators.note: the wine store sits in the future, inside its letters

blocks.note: coming = future, as in the coming year
a bin is a rack for storing wine

annotation.surface: A wine shop's future as it is taken over by another business.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wine store' reads as a shop; a bin is the rack in a cellar.
annotation.definitionFit: Two firms that merge join together into one; the question mark admits the business sense is only one kind of joining.

entries.clue: Pole with blade died, restrained by cleaner in executive suite (9)

indicators.note: someone restrained by another is held in their grip, so these letters sit inside the cleaner

blocks.note: an oar is a pole with a blade
a broom cleans; it holds OARD

annotation.surface: A Pole with a knife died and was seized by a cleaner in the company's top floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pole' at the start of the sentence pretends to be a Polish man; it is a stick.
annotation.definitionFit: Company directors meet around a long table in this room, which the clue calls the suite of the executives.

entries.clue: Squad’s not in contact with Ancient Greek (5)

indicators.note: the squad is not in contact, meaning those letters are absent from it

blocks.note: a platoon is a squad of soldiers
on = touching, in contact with; these letters go

annotation.surface: A sports squad has lost touch with a Greek teammate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Squad’s not' reads as a squad is not; the 's is 'is', and ON is removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Athenian philosopher, pupil of Socrates and teacher of Aristotle.

entries.clue: Stubborn batting contained by over bowled, say (9)

indicators.note: what is contained by something is held within it, so the batting goes inside

blocks.note: a batsman at the crease is in

annotation.surface: A dogged batsman kept quiet through an over before being bowled.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides that 'say' is a verb: state.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone who refuses to change their mind or budge.

entries.clue: Indecent call is a bloomer (8)

blocks.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for to phone them

annotation.surface: A rude phone call is a blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a blunder, but here it is something that blooms.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: anything that flowers is a 'bloomer', and this woodland plant carries nodding violet flowers each spring.

entries.clue: Dash of colour in spun yarn produces striking effect (5)

indicators.note: a dash is only a small amount, so take just the first letter
the colour letter goes in the yarn, inside its letters
a spun yarn is twisted round, so its letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A thread of bright colour in spun wool creates a dramatic look.
annotation.walkthrough: The knitting surface makes yarn wool; it is a story, turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A French borrowing meaning brilliance or dazzling display, the impression of something done with conspicuous flair.

entries.clue: Put in from wing, Batty scored, grabbing second (7)

indicators.note: batty means crazy, and crazy letters are jumbled into a new order
the scored letters grab the second, taking its letter into the mix

blocks.note: S = second, taken into the mix

annotation.surface: A crazy winger crossed the ball and scored within a second.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like a player's name; it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: In football a winger sends the ball across from the side of the pitch into the goalmouth, which is called a cross.

entries.clue: Dissenters on reflection no different in south-west (9)

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so read the whole thing backwards
the no and different words sit in south-west, inside its letters

blocks.note: S for south and W for west, the two compass points; it holds the rest
else = different, as in someone else

annotation.surface: Nonconformists in the West Country who, looking back, were no different after all.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces assemble as S, NAY ELSE, W and then the whole is read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Followers of John Wesley's Methodism broke from the Church of England, and such Protestant nonconformists were called Dissenters.

entries.clue: Girl anything but restrained climbing tree (7)

indicators.note: climbing goes upwards, so in a down clue these letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: OTT = over the top, the opposite of restrained

annotation.surface: A wild girl clambering up a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: An unfamiliar word, so trust the wordplay: ANNA plus OTT reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small tropical American shrub whose red seeds yield an orange food dye used in cheese.

entries.clue: America perhaps putting horse into space? (6)

indicators.note: putting a thing somewhere places it, and the horse is what gets placed
the horse goes into the space, inside its two letters

blocks.note: an em is a printer's space
a pony is a small horse

annotation.surface: A country sending a horse into orbit.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an em is only one kind of space.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the continent takes its name from the explorer Amerigo Vespucci, and a name derived from a person is this.

entries.clue: Stirring up old men, the writer Voltaire, say (3,2,5)

indicators.note: stirring a pot mixes its contents, so the letters are mixed into a new order

annotation.surface: A writer like Voltaire rousing the elders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stirring up' looks like one phrase, but only 'Stirring' is the indicator and UP is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: François-Marie Arouet published under the pen name Voltaire.

entries.clue: One opposing extraordinary action, Conservative must go (4)

indicators.note: the Conservative is told to leave, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: an antic is a grotesque or absurd act

annotation.surface: An opponent of drastic measures says the Tory has to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: The politics hides that 'extraordinary action' is a single thing, an antic.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix meaning against is also used as a noun for a person who objects to some policy.

entries.clue: Like and court nymph at first overcome with emotion (6)

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter of nymph is used

annotation.surface: Falling for a nymph and wooing her until overwhelmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Like and' reads as a pair of verbs; 'like' is as, and 'and' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary adjective for someone in a swoon, fainting or giddy from rapture or feeling.

entries.clue: For light work tree with a pot should be moved (8)

indicators.note: things that are moved change position, so the letters are shifted into a new order

annotation.surface: Advice to a gardener: for an easy job, move the tree and its pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light work' sounds like an easy task; here the work is musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A short comic opera with spoken dialogue, like Gilbert and Sullivan, is a musical work in a lighthearted vein.

entries.clue: A mother needed for man thus deprived? (4)

indicators.note: the pieces are what is required to make the answer, one after the other

blocks.note: a farm animal's mother, as a ewe is to its lamb

annotation.surface: A mother is what a certain motherless man lacked.
annotation.walkthrough: Adam, the first man, had no mother, so he was deprived of the very thing the wordplay supplies.
annotation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first human was formed from dust with no parents, so he alone went without a mother.

entries.clue: Sea round building restricting boy’s interfering (10)

indicators.note: to restrict someone is to hem them in, so the boy sits inside the building

blocks.note: a dome is a round building; it holds LES

annotation.surface: A domed building by the sea hemming in a boy who pokes his nose in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a container indicator but describes the building: a dome.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a busybody who pokes into other people's affairs uninvited is both.
